title: Type Size Explorer
description:
Print a table of every fundamental type with its size and range.
```
Type          Bytes   Min                    Max
char          1       -128                   127
short         2       -32768                 32767
int           4       -2147483648            2147483647
long long     8       -9223372036854775808   9223372036854775807
float         4       1.17549e-38            3.40282e+38
double        8       2.22507e-308           1.79769e+308
```
hints:
`std::setw(n)` from `<iomanip>` pads the **next** thing printed to `n` characters, so it goes before every column. `std::left` puts the padding after the text instead of before, and stays in force until changed:

```cpp
std::cout << std::left << std::setw(6) << "ab" << "|\n";   // prints "ab    |"
```
Every row is the `char` row with the type name changed in three places. Only `char` needs the `static_cast<int>`: without it the limits print as characters.
For `float` and `double`, `min()` is the smallest *positive* value. That is what the sample shows; `lowest()` would give the most negative.
requirements: Use `sizeof` and `std::numeric_limits<T>::min()/max()` (note: for floats `lowest()` is the most negative)
Align columns with `std::setw` (see the first hint)
